mirror_source_reason: Georgia's statute text comes from the Public.Resource.Org / UniCourt mirror (Release 86, 2022.11), not the state's own code host, and later amendments are not reflected.

notices.title: Notice of the contractor's right to resolve construction defects (before a lawsuit)
notices.trigger: Every contract for sale, construction, or improvement of a dwelling by a contractor who must be licensed under Chapter 41 of Title 43
notices.format: Conspicuous; may be part of the contract; substantially the statutory form (printed in capitals)
notices.support: Upon entering into a contract for sale, construction, or improvement of a dwelling
notices.summary_row: Construction-defect notice the contractor must give on entering the contract (NEW, missed by first pass)
notices.block: O.C.G.A. 8-2-41 (notice the contractor must give when the contract is made)

notices.title: Written warranty must be offered on single-family residence contracts over $2,500
notices.trigger: Licensed residential contractor, contract to construct or manage construction of a single-family residence over $2,500
notices.format: Written warranty; see Rule 553-7-.01 for minimum contents
notices.support: Written warranty: 43-41-7 and Rule 553-7-.01 require a licensed residential contractor to offer a written warranty on covered contracts over $2,500.00

notices.title: Written warranty minimum contents; attach before signing
notices.trigger: Licensed residential contractor, covered contract (single-family residence over $2,500)
notices.format: Attach a complete copy of the written warranty (or an identical blank standard form) to the contract or make it available for review before signing
notices.support: attach a complete copy of the written warranty (or an identical blank standard form of it) to the covered contract or otherwise make same available for review
notices.summary_row: Written warranty minimum contents; attach before signing
notices.hold_reason: The rule is a whole regulation (definitions, duty to offer, minimum contents list) with no prescribed warranty wording; printing it would put non-notice rule text in the contract, and whether a remodel or pool is a covered contract is not stated.

notices.title: Repair exemption: written disclosure that the contractor is not licensed
notices.trigger: Repair work done under the repair exemption without a residential or general contractor license
notices.format: Disclosure must be in writing to the owner
notices.support: the person performing the repair work discloses in writing to the owner that such person/entity is not licensed as a residential or general contractor under this chapter
notices.summary_row: Repair exemption: disclosure must be IN WRITING
notices.hold_reason: No prescribed wording; the rule only requires a written disclosure, and the block is a whole rule with other operative conditions (no delegation, no structural work, permits).

changes.new: Federal rule governs most contracts; Georgia O.C.G.A. 10-1-6 gives a right to cancel by midnight of the third business day, but only for a consumer credit sale payable in installments
changes.support: Georgia has one, O.C.G.A. 10-1-6, but it reaches only a "consumer credit sale in which the purchase price is payable in installments" solicited in person and signed at a home

changes.new: Installment credit sales solicited in person and signed at a home (10-1-2(a)(4)); a cash or pay-on-completion job is outside it, so the federal rule (16 CFR 429) still governs
changes.support: A cash or pay-on-completion job is outside it, so the federal rule (16 CFR 429) still governs most contracts.

changes.new: Georgia statute: until 12:00 Midnight of the third business day after the day the buyer signs; notice by certified mail or statutory overnight delivery, return receipt requested; seller may charge 5 percent of the gross sales price or $25.00, whichever is less
changes.support: until 12:00 Midnight of the third business day after the day on which the buyer signs the agreement

changes.new: Disclosure clearly and conspicuously in the contract when a renewal of more than one month takes the contract past six months; reminder 30 to 60 days before the cancellation deadline only for terms of 12 months or more; a violation makes the renewal provision void and unenforceable
changes.support: the 30 to 60 day reminder (13-12-3(a)) applies only to a service contract "for a specified period of 12 months or more". Remedy, which the first pass could not find: 13-12-5, the provision is "void and unenforceable".

unsure: GA-8-2-41: the notice is for contractors who must hold the Chapter 41 license; the builder cannot tell whether a given job needs that license, so applies is left as every contract, but the text is only secondary so nothing prints.
GA-43-41-7 and GA-553-7-01: whether a remodel or pool counts as a covered single-family residence contract is not stated in the file.
Lien waiver and affidavit forms (O.C.G.A. 44-14-366) are handed over at payment, not with the contract, and the file's copy is flattened, so no notice was added for them.
O.C.G.A. 10-1-6 (home solicitation) prescribes no printed statement, so no notice was added.
